Predicates:
CanRegisterToVote(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
ParticipateInElection(x) ::: x can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
HasUSCitizenship(x) ::: x has United States citizenship.
HasTaiwaneseCitizenship(x) ::: x has Taiwanese citizenship.
Official(x) ::: x is a Russian Federation official.
Manager(x, y) ::: x is a manager at y.
RegisterUS(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
Year1946 ::: the year 1946.
Publish(y) ::: y is published in 1946.
Conclusion: 
VladimirIsNotOfficial ::: Vladimir is not a Russian Federation official.

Premises:
∀x (HasUSCitizenship(x) → CanRegisterToVote(x)) ::: If someone has US citizenship, then they can register to vote in the US.
∀x (HasUSCitizenship(x) ∨ HasTaiwaneseCitizenship(x)) ::: Everyone has either US or Taiwanese citizenship.
¬∃x (Official(x) ∧ HasTaiwaneseCitizenship(x)) ::: No Russian Federation official has Taiwanese citizenship.
Vladimir ¬HasTaiwaneseCitizenship ∧ ¬Manager(Vladimir, Gazprom) ::: Vladimir neither holds Taiwanese citizenship nor is he a manager at Gazprom.
Ekaterina (RegisterUS(Ekaterina) ∨ Official(Ekaterina)) ::: Ekaterina can register to vote in the US, or she is a Russian Federation official.
